standard_prerequisites.name: Criterion for a morphism to factor through the closed subscheme cut out by an ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Schemes, Lemma labelled schemes-lemma-characterize-closed-subspace (canonical Stacks tag 01HP); invoked at proof lines 739-741
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the criterion that a morphism factors through the closed subscheme cut out by I as soon as the pullback of I becomes zero; the verification of that vanishing is retained in the counted span.

core_obligations: Set up inside the construction of Z': let U contained in X be the open used to build Z', so that Z is a closed subscheme of U cut out by the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals I; since T and T' have the same underlying topological space the morphism b lands inside U and may be regarded as a morphism into U (proof lines 730-735).

Verify the vanishing that forces the factorisation: let J contained in O_{T'} be the ideal cutting out T; the commutativity of the diagram gives b^#(b^{-1}I) contained in J, and since T contained in T' is a first order thickening we have J^2 = 0, hence b^#(b^{-1}(I^2)) = 0 (proof lines 735-739).

Conclude the universal property: by the factorisation criterion for a closed subscheme cut out by an ideal, b factors through Z' with a unique factorisation a' : T' -> Z', which gives the unique morphism (a', a) : (T contained in T') -> (Z contained in Z') of thickenings over X and proves part (1); the author proves only (1) and refers the higher-order statement to the same pattern (proof lines 739-742).
proof_roadmap: Localise the construction: choose the open U of the construction of Z' with Z closed in U cut out by I, and use |T| = |T'| to regard the given b as a morphism into U (proof lines 730-735).
Compare ideals: the diagram forces b^#(b^{-1}I) contained in J, and square-zero-ness of J for a first order thickening forces b^#(b^{-1}(I^2)) = 0 (proof lines 735-739).

Factor: apply the standard criterion for factoring through the closed subscheme cut out by I to obtain the unique a' : T' -> Z', which is exactly the asserted universal property (proof lines 739-742).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states the universal property of the first order infinitesimal neighbourhood Z' of an immersion i : Z -> X: every commutative diagram with a first order thickening T contained in T' over X admits a unique morphism (a', a) : (T contained in T') -> (Z contained in Z') of thickenings over X, and the analogous statement holds for the n-th order neighbourhood Z_n (statement lines 701-726). The proof converts the universal property into a statement about ideals: after replacing X by the open U in which Z is cut out by I, one shows b^#(b^{-1}I) contained in J, so square-zero-ness of J gives b^#(b^{-1}(I^2)) = 0, and the standard factorisation criterion then produces a' (proof lines 731-741). What makes this non-trivial to guess is that the square-zero hypothesis on the thickening, not merely the diagram, is what makes the factorisation exist at all. The claim is H2; the author proves only part (1) and leaves the higher order statement to the analogous argument, which is reproduced as written.
